meta.name: Editorial Media Application Design Guidelines
meta.sourceDirection: Inspired by the attached mobile streaming browse experience
meta.intent: Create a familiar, content-first software interface that feels editorial, calm, efficient, and native on touch devices without copying any brand-specific assets.

principles: Let content imagery provide most of the color while interface chrome remains neutral.
Use strong hierarchy, generous whitespace, and restrained decoration.
Favor direct manipulation, obvious labels, and familiar platform patterns.
Present collections as horizontally browsable shelves on compact screens and grids on larger screens.
Use a display serif selectively to add editorial character to headings; keep all functional copy in a highly legible sans-serif.
Prefer subtle dividers and tonal surfaces over heavy borders and shadows.
Keep interfaces dense enough to scan quickly but never visually crowded.
avoid: more than one primary action per view
using the display serif for controls or long body copy

headingFont.usage: Page titles, section headings, feature titles, and selected marketing statements

bodyFont.usage: Navigation, controls, labels, metadata, body copy, forms, and data

rules: Use sentence case for headings, labels, tabs, and buttons.
Limit body text lines to 65 to 75 characters.
Truncate card titles after two lines and provide the full title accessibly.
Use tabular numerals for durations, prices, metrics, and tables.

color.strategy: A near-monochrome interface allows artwork, avatars, charts, and status colors to carry emphasis.
usage: Reserve accent color for selected navigation, primary actions, links, and focus.
Never rely on color alone to communicate state.
Maintain WCAG AA contrast for all text and essential controls.
Place text over imagery only with a tested scrim or gradient overlay.

layout.density: Use 8px as the base rhythm, with 4px adjustments for compact metadata.
layout.safeAreas: Respect device safe-area insets for fixed headers, bottom navigation, sheets, and floating actions.

rules: Use small or medium radii on cards and imagery.
Use pill shapes only for chips, compact filters, and statuses.
Use borders for structure and shadows only to establish true elevation.

imagery.style: High-quality, edge-to-edge editorial imagery with consistent crops
imagery.treatment: Use object-fit cover, a subtle radius, and neutral placeholders that preserve layout.
imagery.loading: Use aspect-ratio placeholders to prevent layout shift.

icons.style: Simple outline icons with rounded joins
rules: Use one icon family throughout the product.
Give icon-only buttons accessible names and tooltips.
Do not use emoji as interface icons.

topAppBar.structure: Optional back action, page title, flexible spacer, and up to three priority actions
topAppBar.style: White or translucent surface with a subtle bottom divider when content scrolls beneath it
topAppBar.behavior: May remain sticky; preserve safe-area inset on mobile

globalNavigation.mobile: Use a fixed bottom navigation with 3 to 5 destinations, icon plus label, and a clearly selected state.
globalNavigation.desktop: Use a persistent side rail or header navigation depending on product breadth.
globalNavigation.rules: Do not mix destination navigation with contextual actions.

sidebar.style: Flat neutral surface, grouped links, restrained selected background, and clear collapse behavior

breadcrumbs.usage: Use on deep desktop hierarchies, not as a replacement for mobile back navigation.
breadcrumbs.style: Small secondary text with clear separators and a non-linked current item

tabs.style: Text tabs on a neutral background with a 2px underline for the active tab
tabs.behavior: Allow horizontal scrolling on compact screens and preserve visible focus.
tabs.rules: Use for peer views, not sequential steps.

sectionHeader.structure: Editorial serif heading on the left and an optional concise action such as View all on the right

buttons.primary: Solid accent background, white label, medium radius, semibold text
buttons.secondary: White or subtle surface, 1px border, primary text
buttons.tertiary: Text or icon treatment without a container until hover or focus
buttons.destructive: Danger color; require confirmation only for irreversible or high-impact actions

iconButtons.size: 44px touch target with a 20px to 24px icon
iconButtons.style: Transparent by default; subtle tonal background on hover and press
iconButtons.requirements: Accessible name, visible focus ring, and tooltip on pointer devices

cards.contentCard: Image-first card with title, one metadata line, and optional compact status or action.
cards.listCard: Horizontal layout with thumbnail, title, supporting copy, and trailing action.
cards.dashboardCard: Subtle border, medium radius, no shadow by default, and one clear information purpose.
cards.interaction: If the entire card is interactive, preserve nested action semantics and a visible focus state.

contentShelves.compact: Horizontal scroll with the next item partially visible to signal overflow and scroll snap where helpful.
contentShelves.desktop: Responsive grid with consistent card widths and aligned metadata.
contentShelves.controls: Show previous and next controls only when overflow exists on pointer devices.

forms.fieldStyle: White surface, 1px neutral border, 8px to 10px radius, and a strong accent focus ring
forms.labels: Persistent labels above fields; placeholders provide examples, never labels.
forms.helpText: Place concise guidance below the field.
forms.validation: Show error text beside the field, set aria-invalid, and associate messages programmatically.

search.style: Prominent input with leading search icon, clear action, and optional filter control
search.behavior: Support keyboard submission, recent searches, suggestions, loading, no-results, and error states.

filtersAndChips.style: Compact pill controls with neutral border; selected filters use accent-soft background and accent text.
filtersAndChips.behavior: Make removable chips explicit and provide Clear all when multiple filters are active.

menus.style: Raised white surface, 8px to 12px radius, concise rows, icons only when useful
menus.behavior: Support keyboard navigation, Escape to close, outside click, and collision-aware placement.

tables.style: Quiet horizontal dividers, semibold headers, tabular numerals, and restrained row hover
tables.responsive: Prioritize columns, allow horizontal scrolling, or transform into labeled records on compact screens.
tables.features: Provide sorting, filtering, selection, pagination, loading, empty, and error states when relevant.

lists.style: Use clear row rhythm, aligned leading visuals, concise secondary text, and trailing actions.
lists.states: Selected, unread, disabled, drag, and swipe states must remain distinguishable without color alone.

pagination.style: Use Previous and Next plus nearby page numbers on desktop; use a compact count or load-more pattern on mobile.
pagination.accessibility: Label the navigation region and expose the current page.

dialogs.desktop: Centered modal with constrained width, overlay scrim, clear title, and actions aligned by priority.
dialogs.mobile: Prefer a bottom sheet for short contextual tasks and a full-screen dialog for complex workflows.
dialogs.behavior: Trap focus, close on Escape when safe, restore focus, and prevent background interaction.

drawersAndSheets.style: White elevated surface with 16px to 24px padding and clear drag or close affordance
drawersAndSheets.usage: Filters, contextual details, lightweight editing, and secondary workflows

tooltips.style: Compact dark neutral surface with high-contrast text
tooltips.behavior: Appear after a short delay, remain nonessential, and work with keyboard focus.

notifications.toast: Brief, nonblocking confirmation near the bottom of the viewport; include an action only when immediately useful.
notifications.banner: Full-width contextual message for persistent system or account states.
notifications.alert: Use icon, title, concise explanation, and action; never communicate severity by color alone.

statusIndicators.badges: Compact labels for status or counts, using semantic color plus text or icon.
statusIndicators.progress: Use determinate bars when progress is known and a spinner only for brief indeterminate work.
statusIndicators.skeleton: Mirror final content geometry and avoid excessive shimmer.

emptyErrorAndOfflineStates.empty: Explain why the view is empty and offer one useful next action.
emptyErrorAndOfflineStates.error: State what failed in plain language and provide retry or recovery.
emptyErrorAndOfflineStates.offline: Preserve available content, identify stale data, and explain which actions require a connection.

mediaControls.style: High-contrast controls over a scrim, large central primary action, and persistent time indicators
mediaControls.requirements: Keyboard controls, captions, transcript support where appropriate, volume, playback speed, and fullscreen.

dataVisualization.style: Use the neutral palette as a base and a limited accessible categorical palette.
dataVisualization.requirements: Provide labels, legends, summaries, keyboard access where interactive, and a nonvisual data alternative.

authentication.layout: Single focused column with a concise heading, clear fields, primary submit action, and secondary recovery links
authentication.rules: Support password managers, reveal-password controls, useful errors, and no unnecessary friction.

commandPalette.style: Centered elevated search surface with grouped results and visible keyboard shortcuts
commandPalette.behavior: Full keyboard operation, fuzzy search, recent actions, and Escape to close

rules: Animate opacity and transform rather than layout properties.
Use motion to explain hierarchy, state change, or spatial continuity.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion and remove nonessential movement.

touch.spacing: Keep at least 8px between adjacent targets.
touch.gestures: Never make a gesture the only way to complete an action.

interaction.feedback: Every action should produce immediate visual feedback; optimistic updates must provide recovery when failure is possible.

requirements: Provide a logical heading hierarchy and landmark structure.
Support full keyboard operation and visible focus.
Maintain at least 4.5:1 contrast for normal text and 3:1 for large text and interface boundaries.
Provide text alternatives for meaningful imagery and empty alt text for decorative imagery.
Do not encode meaning through color, position, or motion alone.
Announce asynchronous updates through appropriate live regions.
Support 200 percent text zoom without loss of content or function.
Respect reduced motion, increased contrast, and device text-size preferences.

compact: Use horizontal content shelves and bottom navigation.
Move secondary workflows into sheets or full-screen views.
Keep the primary action reachable without covering content.
tablet: Introduce two-column layouts where content benefits.
Allow a navigation rail and larger content cards.
Use modal dialogs for focused tasks.
desktop: Use responsive grids and persistent navigation.
Constrain reading width even when the viewport is wide.
Expose hover affordances without making them necessary.
Use density controls only for data-heavy workflows.

implementationChecklist: Load DM Serif Display and Inter from Google Fonts with font-display swap.
Define all visual values as reusable design tokens.
Build and test every component state, including loading, empty, error, disabled, and focus.
Verify layouts at compact, tablet, and desktop breakpoints.
Test keyboard navigation, screen reader labels, text zoom, contrast, and reduced motion.
Use real-world long labels and missing-image cases during QA.
Avoid using copyrighted logos, artwork, or exact brand-specific visual assets from the reference.
